translations.text: The martyrdom of the holy and glorious martyr Archil, who was king of Kartli. When fifty years had passed in this time, Chichnaom, son of Muhammad, came again.
He laid waste to and destroyed everything that had been built in Kartli, and he set out to enter Kakheti, so that he might lay it waste and leave it entirely without inhabitants.
The kings, the princes and all the people were in great fear, and they could not resist him,
for ever since the Deaf One had ravaged this land, it had not recovered its former state, even though long periods had passed in peace.
But the holy Archil made a resolution in his heart, out of the courage of his heart:
he would go and see him and ask him for peace for the land, for the churches to be protected and left unharmed, and for an end to the pressure on the people to abandon their faith.
Trusting in God, he chose to lay down his own life and soul as a ransom for the Christians. He rose and went to Chichanaum, who was called Asim.
When Asim learned that he was coming, he went out joyfully to meet him and greeted him with great honour. They spent that day together.
Asim praised his goodness. He took a liking to his full-grown stature, and still more to the beauty of his face.
After a few days he began to speak to him with flattery. He promised him great gifts and urged him to abandon the faith of Christ and
to convert to the Saracens. But the holy Archil would not accept his deceit at all. With a firm mind he answered him and said:
"Far be it from me to listen to your words, or to abandon Christ the living God, who is the true God,
who endured death in the flesh for our salvation. If I listen to you, know that I would die a death by which I would be tormented for ever.
But if you kill me, I will rise again like my God and will also be glorified with him."
When the lawless man heard all this and saw his unwavering firmness, he was greatly amazed.

He ordered him to be seized and put in prison, so that he might bring him over by some scheme, for he did not want him put to death, because of the beauty of his appearance and the height of his stature.
When they had put him in prison, Archil blessed God and asked Him for help,
so that in His mercy He would make him worthy to reach the endless light and live there for ever with all the saints, who gained immortality by dying for God.
Then a certain prince from Gardabani, who had converted to the Saracens, came before Asim.
The Tsanars had killed his paternal uncle, and the killers had escaped safely to Archil's grandfather, King Adarnase.
Because of this, the man from Gardabani held a grudge, and he said to Asim: "Do you not know who this Archil is?
He is the son of Stephen and a kinsman of the great king Vakhtang, who was of the line of Mirian, son of Chosroes.
He was with his father when they buried the royal treasures of Kartli. He also knows
where King Heraclius buried his treasures, because Heraclius too showed them where they were burying them."
When Asim heard this, he summoned Archil again and said to him: "Before, I was lenient with you because of your good looks, for you are very handsome,
"But now I have been told about you, that you are a son of the great Khosroid kings. Now you will become even greater in my sight,
if you obey me. Your kingdom will stay your own, and I will also grant you the treasuries of your fathers.
First show me the treasuries of the kings of the Greeks, and convert to my faith.
Become a Saracen, and I will make you spasalar (commander-in-chief) over the land of Kartli, king and lord over the peoples of Kartli."
Then holy Archil answered: "Know for certain that I was young in age when King Heraclius passed through this land.
My father and my brother put all their treasures in the fortress where the Deaf Emir turned back.
Now the Greeks have it. But I will not forsake the Lord my God, nor will I sell that glory which does not pass away for this one which quickly passes."
Asim answered and said: "So you were there at that defeat in Abkhazia?" Saint Archil said to him:
"I was there at the time when God struck them down." Asim said to him: "Which God struck down the Saracens?" Saint Archil answered and said to him:
"The living God, who is the creator of heaven and earth, and who came down from heaven to earth for the salvation of the human race,
[?] "...and by his own death he raised us up and granted us immortality. So it was he who struck them down and humbled them." Then Asim said to Saint Archil:
"So the one whose God is mortal, and you who place your hope of life in a mortal — it is fitting that he too should die."
And he ordered that holy Archil be put to death by beheading. He showed no regard for Archil's goodness, and he was not ashamed before the glory of his high rank.
They led him outside and cut off his head with a sword in the month of Mirkani, which is March, on the twentieth of that month. And
he commended his soul into the hands of the Creator. He chose death, which wins immortality.
He exchanged this short-lived kingship of the passing world for eternal joy.
He was found worthy to stand before God among the ranks of the saints and valiant martyrs, and with them, wearing a crown, he rejoices before the Holy Trinity.
When the holy martyr Archil had died, the Goderdziani of Tbeti came that night, and with them other [?] nobles (mameani, perhaps "hereditary"). They stole the body of the holy martyr Archil.
They carried it off, [?] it with great honour (the text has "shattered/crushed", probably a corruption, perhaps for "clothed" or "adorned"), and buried it at Notkora, in the church that he had built.
His wife granted villages in Kakheti as a hereditary estate to those who had brought back the body of the holy martyr Archil.
This book of his martyrdom was found written down very briefly. Because of the disorder of the times, no one had been able to write it as it ought to have been written.
This book of the Life of the Georgians was written down from time to time up to the time of Vakhtang.
From King Vakhtang until now it was written by Juansher Juansheriani, the husband of holy Archil's niece (his brother's daughter), of the lineage of Rev, son of Mirian.
From then on, the generations that come after will write as they see, and as the present time makes things known to their God-enlightened minds.
